title: The Gift That Is Not Accepted
text:
A brahmin of the Bharadvaja clan was furious when he heard that one of his clan had left home to become a monk under the Buddha. He went to find the Buddha and abused him to his face with rude and harsh words.

The Buddha waited until he had finished. Then he asked a question. "Brahmin, do friends and relatives come to visit you as guests?" "Yes, sometimes." "And do you offer them food and refreshments?" "Yes, I do." "And if they do not accept them, to whom do those things belong?" "If they do not accept them, they remain mine."

"In the same way," said the Buddha, "you have abused me, who does not abuse, and scolded me, who does not scold. I do not accept it. It is all yours, brahmin, it belongs to you." He explained that one who answers abuse with abuse is like a guest sharing the meal, while one who does not repay anger with anger wins a battle hard to win.

The brahmin was taken aback. According to the sutta, he asked to become a monk himself, was accepted, and in time reached the goal of the holy life.
lesson: Insults only hurt you if you take them in. You can decline to pick up someone's anger and let it stay with them.
people: The Buddha, the brahmin Akkosaka Bharadvaja
